title: Monetized publish allowed when the data lineage class is not legal
body:
## Summary
The gate checked only data.sources[] for licence class; manifest.data.license_class (the lineage's most restrictive class, 'unknown' when a view has no lineage row) was never read, so a non-legal or unknown lineage passed on a monetized target.

## Description
apps/server/src/warehouse.ts:193-200 computes data.license_class as the most restrictive class over the views ("unknown" when a view has no meta.model_lineage row); apps/server/src/pipeline.ts:368 keeps in sources[] only lineage sources that have a snapshot row, so a source can drop out of sources[] while the class still carries it. policy/publish.rego source_not_legal_on_monetized read only sources[]. Registry: quality-gates / unmeasurable-criteria (missing evidence blocks, never skips). Fixed: rule data_license_not_legal_on_monetized (policy/publish.rego:141) denies when monetized and the class is not 'legal' (missing = unknown).

## Flow
- a view the video reads has no lineage row -> lineage returns 'unknown'
- its sources are legal or have no snapshot -> sources[] all legal
- monetized target -> gate ALLOW (before) / DENY 'data license class unknown: not allowed on a monetized channel' (after)

## Expected impact
A monetized publish can no longer ride on unknown or non-commercial lineage. Could break: a render whose lineage is legitimately incomplete now denies until `just transform` records it (0 of 21 local render manifests affected).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the gate denies every non-legal lineage on a monetized target
Before: opa probe on the test sample, monetized: allow=true for license_class unknown / non_commercial / paid / missing (4 of 4)
After: allow=false for all 4, legal still allow=true; 21 of 21 real manifests carry 'legal' (0 new denies)
Method: gate - 6 new rego tests red-then-green plus the probe above; pnpm check --only opa 112/112
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
policy/publish.rego:141-150 (new rule)
apps/server/src/warehouse.ts:193-200 (lineage: most restrictive, 'unknown' on a missing row)
apps/server/src/pipeline.ts:368 (sources[] filtered to lineage sources with a snapshot)
coupled: apps/studio/src/studio/deny-hints.ts (hint; deny-hints.test.ts reads the rego)
instrument: policy/publish_test.rego data_license_* tests (6) + opa probe over license_class values

title: A 308 that keeps nothing of a chunk made the uploader loop forever
body:
## Summary
uploadChunks treated every 308 as progress and reset its retry counter, so a session that answers 308 without advancing resent the same 8 MiB chunk in a tight loop with no sleep and no bound.

## Description
packages/publish/src/youtube.ts:388 (before the fix) set offset from the Range header and attempt=0 on every 308. Registry: retry-backoff / backoff-design ('backoff resets on every accepted handshake'; a stated reset is not recovery). Fixed: a 308 counts as progress only when the committed offset moves past the one just sent; otherwise it backs off and spends maxRetries, then throws YouTubeApiError 'chunk upload made no progress at byte N'.

## Flow
- init POST -> session
- first chunk -> 308 bytes=0-262143 (progress)
- every later PUT -> the same 308 -> before: resend forever, 0 sleeps; after: backoff 2/4/8 s, then throw

## Expected impact
A misbehaving proxy or server can no longer pin a publish job in a hot loop burning bandwidth. Could break: nothing on the progress path (existing 308/503 resume test unchanged).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a non-advancing resumable session ends in a bounded error
Before: new test, maxRetries 3: 60 requests with 0 sleeps until the test's runaway cap threw
After: 6 requests (init, landed chunk, 1 + 3 stalled resends), sleeps [2000, 4000, 8000], then the no-progress error
Method: gate - youtube.test.ts case red-then-green; vitest packages/publish 59/59
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/publish/src/youtube.ts:388-402 (308 branch after fix)
packages/publish/src/youtube.test.ts 'a 308 that keeps nothing of the chunk spends the retry budget...'
instrument: youtube.test.ts stall case with a runaway cap (seeded red on the old code)

title: defaultOpaBin ignored the .tools/opa that setup installs off Windows
body:
## Summary
scripts/setup-tools.mjs installs .tools/opa on every platform and scripts/check.mjs runs it, but defaultOpaBin() used it only on win32 and spawned a bare `opa` from PATH elsewhere.

## Description
packages/publish/src/policy.ts defaultOpaBin (now :38) returned 'opa' off Windows; scripts/setup-tools.mjs:23 and scripts/check.mjs:69 use .tools/opa[.exe] everywhere. On macOS/Linux after `just setup`, `pnpm check --only opa` passes while evaluatePolicy's default fails with ENOENT. Fixed: OPA_BIN, else .tools/opa[.exe] (always on win32, off Windows when it exists), else PATH. A third copy remains in apps/server/src/pipeline.ts:475 (carded separately, out of scope).

## Flow
- linux: just setup -> .tools/opa
- evaluatePolicy() default -> spawn 'opa' -> ENOENT (before) / .tools/opa (after)

## Expected impact
The package's gate runner finds the same binary the repo gate uses on every OS. Could break: nothing on Windows (unchanged path).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one OPA resolution rule across setup, check and the runner
Before: linux/darwin with .tools/opa present -> 'opa' (2 of 4 platform cases wrong; the function took no inputs so the cases could not be expressed)
After: 4 of 4 platform cases + OPA_BIN precedence
Method: gate - policy.test.ts defaultOpaBin cases red-then-green (tsc also red before: the signature took no args)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/publish/src/policy.ts:34-46
scripts/setup-tools.mjs:23
scripts/check.mjs:69
apps/server/src/pipeline.ts:475 (third copy, untouched)

title: Gate accepted any plan_tier string; 'Free' or 'trial' cleared the free-plan rule
body:
## Summary
The schema's PlanTier enum and the audio client reject unknown tiers, but the gate accepted any non-empty string and denied only the exact spelling 'free', so 'Free', 'FREE', 'trial' passed on a monetized target.

## Description
packages/schemas/src/index.ts:267 PlanTier and packages/audio/src/plan-tier.ts (throws on 'trial') vs policy/publish.rego valid_plan_tier (non-empty string). policyCheck reads manifest.json unparsed, so a hand-edited or legacy manifest reaches the gate as-is. Fixed: plan_tiers = the enum (policy/publish.rego:129); audio_missing_plan_tier gains an annotated second body '<kind> audio has unknown plan_tier <tier>'; policy.test.ts pins rego plan_tiers == PlanTier.options.

## Flow
- manifest audio[].plan_tier = 'Free' on a monetized target
- before: no deny, allow=true
- after: 'music audio has unknown plan_tier Free', allow=false

## Expected impact
A non-commercial take cannot pass the monetized gate by spelling. Could break: a manifest with a tier outside the 7-value enum now denies (21 of 21 local manifests use 'starter').

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the gate and the schema accept the same tier vocabulary
Before: opa probe, monetized sample: allow=true for Free / FREE / trial / free_trial (4 of 4 off-vocabulary)
After: allow=false for all 4; the 6 paid enum tiers allow; 'free' still denies; seeded drop of 'starter' turns both the rego valid sample and the TS parity test red
Method: gate - rego tests + TS parity test red-then-green; opa 115/115
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
instrument: publish_test.rego unknown/known plan tier tests + policy.test.ts 'policy/publish.rego plan_tiers'

title: checks_run guarded only by its own count
body:
## Summary
publish.rego's hand-written checks_run list and its claim 'every rule name appears in exactly one deny/warn rule' were guarded only by count == 27 in two tests that read the list itself.

## Description
policy/publish_test.rego test_checks_run_lists_every_rule and packages/publish/src/policy.test.ts compared the list's length to a literal. Interrogate-the-hand-list rule (§4.7). Fixed: policy.test.ts parses publish.rego - checks_run equals the `# rule:` annotations, every deny/warn body carries its own annotation directly above it, every rule has a section in publish_test.rego - and the real-opa test compares the gate's checks_run with the parsed list. 6b65517 tightened the instrument after a seed showed an unannotated `deny contains msg if {` placed after another rule passed.

## Flow
- add a deny without listing it, rename a list entry, or drop a test section
- before: opa 106/106 and vitest green
- after: the checks_run tests go red

## Expected impact
The gate's self-report (checks_run, shown in the studio as 'Checks run · N') cannot drift from its rules unnoticed. Could break: nothing - tests only plus one rego annotation.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - drift between checks_run and the rule bodies is caught
Before: 0 of 4 seeded drifts caught (rename keeping the count; unannotated literal deny; unannotated generic deny mid-file; dropped test section)
After: 4 of 4 red; restored tree green
Method: gate - seeded violations against both suites
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/publish/src/policy.test.ts regoRules() + 'policy/publish.rego checks_run' block
policy/publish.rego:13-14, 269-283 (duration_out_of_band: both bodies annotated)

title: authorize() untested and left its 5-minute timer armed on a failed open
body:
## Summary
The interactive OAuth path - loopback listener plus CSRF state check - had no tests, and its timeout was cleared only when a callback arrived, so an openBrowser failure left a 5-minute timer holding the process open.

## Description
packages/publish/src/oauth.ts authorize() cleared its timer inside the request handler only; Promise.resolve(open(...)).catch(rej) rejected without clearing it. Fixed: timer declared outside the promise and cleared in the finally that closes the server. Tests drive authorize() on a real 127.0.0.1 listener with fetch mocked (no Google): forged state -> 400 + state_mismatch + no token request; right state -> code exchanged with the PKCE verifier and exact redirect; failed open -> 0 pending timers.

## Flow
- CLI connect -> openBrowser throws (no browser)
- authorize() rejects
- before: process stays alive 5 more minutes; after: exits

## Expected impact
A failed connect step exits when it reports; the state check is pinned. Could break: nothing (timer cleared on paths that already settled).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - every exit of authorize() releases its timer; the CSRF check is covered
Before: 1 pending timer after the failed authorize(); 0 tests over authorize()
After: 0 pending timers; 3 authorize tests, 12/12 oauth tests stable over 3 runs
Method: gate - fake-timer count red-then-green
Result: better
Gate: none

title: SETUP.md and a test comment claimed wiring that does not exist
body:
## Summary
SETUP.md promised that after connecting, `pnpm e2e:live` uploads, verifies and deletes a private video; policy.test.ts said CI/`just check` set OPA_REQUIRED=1. Neither is true.

## Description
packages/publish/SETUP.md step 5: no TokenProvider is passed to YouTubeClient anywhere in apps/server (live mode throws without one) and e2e/m1.spec.ts publishes dry. packages/publish/src/policy.test.ts:31: there is no CI and scripts/check.mjs never sets OPA_REQUIRED. Both rewritten to state what the tree does.

## Flow
- owner finishes SETUP step 4-5 -> runs pnpm e2e:live expecting a live upload -> gets a dry run

## Expected impact
The owner is not told a live run exists that does not. Could break: nothing (text).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - package copy matches the code
Before: 2 statements asserting behaviour the tree lacks
After: 0
Method: probe - grep TokenProvider/tokenProvider in apps/server (0 sites) and OPA_REQUIRED repo-wide (test + API-NOTES only)
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Publish job trusts the render-time verdict; the attribution warn can never fire
body:
## Summary
The gate runs at render time with a target that cannot carry a description, and the publish job builds the description later without re-gating, so description_missing_attribution is vacuous and a verdict that predates a policy change is still honoured.

## Description
packages/schemas/src/index.ts:315 PublishTargetSchema has no description field; apps/server/src/pipeline.ts:423 publishes on the stored policy_json.allow; :427 assembles the final description afterwards. policy/publish.rego:354 (warn) needs input.target.description. Registry: quality-gates / vacuous-by-evaluation. Fix: publishJob re-evaluates the gate with { ...stored target, description } immediately before upload, refusing on deny and recording warns; PublishTargetSchema gains optional description.

## Flow
- render gated ALLOW with the produce target
- publish job builds description from p.description + method_note + attributions
- gate never sees it; a later rego tightening is not applied either

## Expected impact
Attribution loss becomes visible and stale ALLOWs stop publishing. Could break: renders allowed under an older policy now refuse until re-produced.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the gate judges what is actually published
Before: 0 of 1 publish paths evaluate the final description; warn reachable from product: 0
After: 1 of 1 (predicted)
Method: simulation - seam is apps/server (pipeline) + packages/schemas, other contexts; three cases: description edited to drop credit, rego tightened after render, default description
Result: better
Gate: contract
instrument: pipeline.test.ts: publish job with a policy_json allow + a manifest the current rego denies -> expect Refusal; a description without the attribution -> expect warn recorded

title: Gate thresholds live only in rego; the studio re-types them (45-75 s card)
body:
## Summary
The studio checks table judges duration on 45-75 s and shows no black-frame limit while publish.rego denies outside 30-90 s and above 1 s; the policy publishes no thresholds for a surface to read.

## Description
Judged from the policy side for compose-render-gate-ui's open card: publish.rego is correct (DESIGN §2 D16 / ADR 007: 30-90 s; DESIGN.md:314 45-75 s is a use-case editorial band, not a gate). The structural fix on this side: export the thresholds (duration_band_s, max_black_s, loudness, true peak, cps, allowed_resolutions, target_fps) as a `limits` object in POLICY_QUERY so RenderGatePage reads the gate's own numbers. Registry: quality-gates / policy-projection. Touches packages/publish/src/policy.ts (query), PolicyResultSchema (packages/schemas), apps/studio logic.ts.

## Flow
- 80 s render -> gate ALLOW
- studio Duration row FAIL (45-75 s)
- after: row reads limits.duration 30-90 PASS; use-case band shown as an editorial target

## Expected impact
Table verdicts equal gate verdicts. Could break: PolicyResult consumers (schema gains an optional field).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one source for gate thresholds
Before: 7 thresholded rows hand-copied in the studio; 2 disagree (duration, black frames)
After: 0 hand copies (predicted)
Method: simulation - spans schemas + studio, other contexts
Result: better
Gate: contract
instrument: policy.test.ts: limits from evaluatePolicy equal the rego constants; studio logic test: checkRows uses limits

title: Safe-zone deny cannot name the line: the rego side needs an evidence field
body:
## Summary
Judged for captions' open card: the rego deny is the fixed string 'safe-zone violations' because the manifest carries only a count; naming the line needs an optional evidence array the rule can read, and nothing in policy.ts.

## Description
policy/publish.rego:302-307 reads checks.safe_zone_violations (a number). Policy-side need: when checks.safe_zone_offenders (e.g. [{t_s, text}]) is present, the deny message becomes 'safe-zone violations: <n> lines, first at <t> s: "<text>"'; the count stays required evidence. packages/publish/src/policy.ts needs no change (deny strings pass through). The studio hint regex /^safe-zone violations$/ (apps/studio/src/studio/deny-hints.ts) must become a prefix match. Depends on the captions/server/schemas change named in captions.jsonl.

## Flow
- render overflows one caption line
- deny 'safe-zone violations'
- after: deny names the cue time and text

## Expected impact
The operator goes straight to the offending cue. Could break: deny-hint regex and calendar tests that match the exact string.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a failure carries the evidence that explains it
Before: 0 of 1 deny paths name the cue
After: 1 of 1 (predicted)
Method: simulation - the evidence producer is in other contexts
Result: better
Gate: contract
instrument: publish_test.rego: offenders present -> message names the first; absent -> legacy message

title: A '<' or '>' in title or method_note passes the gate, fails at upload
body:
## Summary
validateSnippet refuses '<'/'>' and over-length titles, but the props schema and the gate never check them, so an ALLOWed render fails at publish after the calendar fired.

## Description
packages/publish/src/youtube.ts:199-209 validateSnippet; packages/schemas/src/index.ts:144 method_note is z.string().min(1); apps/server/src/pipeline.ts:427 joins method_note into the description; :434 slices the title by UTF-16 units (can split a surrogate pair) while validateSnippet counts code points. Fix: export a snippet check (or sanitizer) the compose/props step runs, so the failure surfaces before the gate.

## Flow
- co-pilot writes method_note 'drivers with <5 starts excluded'
- render gated ALLOW
- scheduled publish -> uploadVideo throws 'title/description may not contain < or >'

## Expected impact
Publish failures move to compose time. Could break: props that pass today fail validation.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a publish-blocking defect is caught before the gate
Before: checks for '<'/'>' before upload: 0
After: 1 (predicted)
Method: simulation - seam is schemas/pipeline; walked: '<' in method_note, 101-char emoji title, 5001-byte description
Result: better
Gate: contract
instrument: schemas test: method_note with '<' rejected; pipeline test: title clamp by code points

title: A 401 mid-upload fails the job instead of refresh-then-retry-once
body:
## Summary
retryable() treats 401 as permanent, so an access token revoked or expired early during a long upload fails the job though one refresh would succeed.

## Description
packages/publish/src/youtube.ts retryable() (:478-489) returns undefined for 401 and ensureOk throws; TokenProvider (packages/publish/src/oauth.ts:13-15) has no way to drop a cached token. Registry: retry-backoff / error-classification-for-retry ('auth-expired is repair-then-retry-once, not a ladder'). Fix: optional TokenProvider.invalidate(); send() on 401 invalidates, refetches the token and retries once. Note: distinct from the deferred OAuth custody items (revoke, keychain adapter, single-flight refresh) - live mode is not wired yet, so this lands dormant.

## Flow
- upload hour 2, token revoked server-side -> chunk PUT 401
- before: job fails, session file kept
- after: refresh + one retry continues the session

## Expected impact
Long live uploads survive a token rotation. Could break: a provider without invalidate() keeps today's behaviour.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - auth expiry is repaired once, not fatal
Before: 401 -> immediate failure (mocked)
After: 401 then 200 -> success with 1 refresh (predicted)
Method: simulation - M across oauth.ts + youtube.ts; interface change deserves its own isolated run
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: youtube.test.ts: 401 then 308/200 with a provider counting invalidate() calls

title: Uploads retry 5xx/429/quota; captions, list, get and stats calls never do
body:
## Summary
The same transient outage is retried on videos.insert and dropped on captions.insert, captions.list, videos.list and stats, and captions.insert (400 units, not idempotent) has no dedupe story for a retry.

## Description
packages/publish/src/youtube.ts:493-526 insertCaptions, :528-597 list/get/delete/stats call send() once and ensureOk. Registry: retry-backoff / error-classification-for-retry ('same outage retried by one path and dropped by another'; 'a timed-out write needs an idempotency story'). Fix: retry the GETs with the existing ladder; for captions.insert, list-then-insert (skip when a track with the language exists) before any retry.

## Flow
- upload succeeds
- captions.insert -> 503
- before: publish job fails after the video exists (the orphan case reserved in the pipeline note)

## Expected impact
A transient 5xx after upload no longer fails the publish. Could break: a retried captions.insert could duplicate a track without the list check.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - one classification for all adapter calls
Before: retrying call sites: 3 of 8 (init, chunk, probe)
After: 8 of 8 with captions dedupe (predicted)
Method: simulation - needs a mocked-fetch matrix; M
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: youtube.test.ts matrix: each call with 503 then 200; captions.insert with an existing track -> no second insert

title: send() copies every 8 MiB chunk before handing it to fetch
body:
## Summary
new Uint8Array(buf) copies the chunk buffer, so each PUT allocates the chunk twice.

## Description
packages/publish/src/youtube.ts:652 wraps the Buffer in new Uint8Array(...), which copies. A view (new Uint8Array(b.buffer, b.byteOffset, b.byteLength)) or the Buffer itself avoids it, if the BodyInit typing accepts it under the repo's TS lib.

## Flow
- upload of a 200 MB render at 8 MiB chunks -> 25 extra 8 MiB allocations

## Expected impact
Lower peak memory during uploads. Could break: tsc on BodyInit typing.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - one allocation per chunk
Before: 2 allocations of chunk size per PUT (read buffer + copy)
After: 1 (predicted)
Method: simulation - needs a heap/ArrayBuffer-count probe and a tsc check
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: youtube.test.ts: the body passed to fetch shares its ArrayBuffer with the read buffer

title: An upload that comes back non-private is left on the channel
body:
## Summary
uploadVideo throws when YouTube returns a privacyStatus other than private, but the video stays live at that visibility; no remediation runs.

## Description
packages/publish/src/youtube.ts:327-333 throws YouTubeApiError after the upload completed. Remediation (videos.update to private, or delete) acts on the live channel and on what is publicly visible - operator-only under CLAUDE.md ('anything that becomes publicly visible'). The adapter always sends private and unaudited projects are forced private, so the trigger is unlikely; the consequence is a public video.

## Flow
- upload with privacyStatus private
- API returns public (channel default / API change)
- adapter throws; the video remains public

## Expected impact
Closes the one path where v1 could leave something public. Could break: a remediation call that fails leaves the same state plus noise.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a visibility mismatch is remediated, not only reported
Before: remediation calls after a non-private response: 0
After: 1 (videos.update private, then re-check)
Method: simulation - live-API behaviour; an operator decides remediation (update vs delete)
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: irreversible
instrument: mocked-fetch test of the remediation call; the policy (update vs delete) is the owner's

title: Add jitter to the upload backoff ladder
body:
## Summary
retry-backoff / backoff-design asks for jittered backoff; the adapter's ladder is deterministic (2^n s, capped 64 s).

## Description
packages/publish/src/youtube.ts:469-472. Jitter decorrelates many callers retrying one dependency; this adapter has one upload in flight per publish job and one process, so there is no herd to break up. Rejected as churn.

## Flow
- one publish job -> one uploader -> one retry ladder

## Expected impact
None measurable; adds nondeterminism to tests that pin sleeps.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - fewer synchronized retries
Before: concurrent uploaders per process: 1 (synchronized retry pulses: 1 caller)
After: 1 caller (jitter changes nothing measurable)
Method: probe - counted uploaders per process from apps/server publishJob
Result: not-better
Gate: none
